title: EIP-8025: Optional Execution Proofs
summary: Normally every validator must replay each block's transactions against the full Ethereum state to check it is valid - costly work that grows with the gas limit. This feature lets volunteer nodes produce small cryptographic proofs that others can verify cheaply, without holding the state. It is fully opt-in and changes no consensus rules.
impacts: No direct impact; the mechanism is opt-in and changes no consensus rules, transaction behaviour, or fees.
No impact; introduces no new opcodes, gas changes, or contract-level semantics.
No impact; no transaction format or RPC changes affecting wallets.
New proof-node and prover infrastructure, plus gossip and req/resp tooling, needed to generate, serve, and verify execution proofs.
L2s reusing the maturing stateless guest, witness format, and proving stack could benefit, though nothing is required of them.
Opt-in: proof-verifying nodes gain additional stateless validation; proof-generating nodes take on extra bandwidth and proving costs.
Substantial opt-in work: new gossip topic, ProofEngine interface, req/resp protocols, ENR key, and an out-of-state-transition proof handler.
Implement the stateless guest program, execution witness construction, SSZ stateless input/output schema, and host-side input assembly.
